# Phase Two — Architecture, File Map, and Twenty Improvements

The Awtsmoos draws a line from canonical source to living post without division or disguise;
Awtsmoos.com should make each module small enough that future eyes can see why it exists and where it lies.

## Observed code facts

- `modules/chitas/*` already creates a virtual Daily Chitas series.
- `living-path/cards.js` contains an explicit Chabad.org external redirect and suppresses social actions for `virtualStudy`.
- `api/comments.js` already supports `verseSection`, which can anchor verse-level discussion without inventing a second comment API.
- Normal post cards navigate to `/heichelos/{heichel}/series/{series}/{post}`.
- A new Torah Library layer exists with `torahLibrary.js`, `torahLibraryIds.js`, and `torahLibraryPresentation.js`, but it currently models root/domain/work/page virtual bookshelf IDs, not a generic verse-range post abstraction.
- No existing `dynamicPost`, `referencePost`, `contentRefs`, or range-reference abstraction was found.

## Proposed module graph

`dynamic-reference/reference-contract.js`
→ validates ordered source references and stable identity.

`dynamic-reference/reference-id.js`
→ creates/parses URL-safe dynamic post IDs.

`dynamic-reference/reference-registry.js`
→ dispatches a reference to a source adapter.

`dynamic-reference/post-composer.js`
→ resolves ordered ranges and returns a normal post-like reader model.

`chitas/range-reference.js`
→ converts aliyah boundary metadata into canonical Tanach-range references.

`chitas/week-state.js`
→ URL/query date, language, Israel/Diaspora, previous/next/today helpers.

`chitas/dynamic-post.js`
→ reconstructs one Chitas dynamic post from stable post ID + query state.

`chitas/week-controls.js`
→ pure control model for UI renderers.

Existing `chitas/schedule.js` and `virtual-series.js`
→ produce native internal cards and selected-week data, never external URLs.

Existing `living-path/cards.js`
→ delete the Chabad-specific branch; Chitas follows normal post navigation/social.

Normal post reader entry
→ intercept `daily-chitas` dynamic IDs and obtain post body through `post-composer`; all ordinary posts untouched.

## Exact likely touched files

New modules under `geelooy/heichelos/heichel/modules/dynamic-reference/` and `modules/chitas/`. Existing Chitas schedule/series/card renderer. One reader/router integration file once located by direct route inspection. Focused CSS modules for Chitas week controls/reader masthead if the reader has modular style manifests. Tests under `tests/geelooy/`.

## Twenty-plus concrete improvements over phase one

1. Keep source reference shape independent from Chitas.
2. Keep calendar date outside canonical Torah range identity where possible.
3. Use stable dynamic post ID as the comment-thread post identity.
4. Preserve `verseSection` for comments bound to canonical verses.
5. Never encode human language labels as source keys.
6. Separate resolver errors from scheduler errors.
7. Make language a presentation/resolution option, not a different Torah identity.
8. Keep Israel/Diaspora in week state because it changes schedule selection.
9. Normalize all date math at local noon to avoid UTC day drift.
10. Make previous/next week exactly ±7 local days.
11. Make Today remove stale date override instead of accumulating query cruft.
12. Maintain direct-reload URLs after every selector change.
13. Make the week list chronologically Sunday→Shabbos.
14. Highlight selected day separately from today.
15. Keep card social actions available because the card is now a normal post.
16. Ensure card click never reads `externalHref`.
17. Use the normal comments API; no Chitas-specific backend comments endpoint.
18. Compose content from canonical source records rather than copy/paste Torah text into the Chitas object.
19. Provide source provenance in the reader UI without exposing external study destinations.
20. Cache at resolver boundary, not schedule boundary.
21. Add `AbortController` to asynchronous source resolution.
22. Keep every new JS/CSS module under 120 lines.
23. Add explicit B"H / Boruch Hashem / Blessed is He poetic module headers.
24. Use tabs in every touched source file.
25. No partial modifications: every existing touched file is rewritten completely.
26. Test normal non-Chitas post cards after removing the special external branch.
27. Test comments visibility on dynamic Chitas posts.
28. Test hard reload of a deep Chitas post URL.
29. Test share/copy URL reconstructs same week/language.
30. Test graceful internal error if Torah source resolution fails.

## Dependency graph

Schedule metadata → Chitas range adapter → generic reference contract → source resolver → post composer → existing reader → existing comments/social.

Week query state → Chitas series loader + reader masthead.

Living Path cards → normal internal post route → same dynamic reconstruction path on click or reload.

The critical invariant is one-way: no dynamic post may become the canonical Torah source. The canonical source feeds the composed vessel; the vessel never owns the Torah it reveals.
